responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The compact example clearly explains how reciprocal absolute entitlements can empower blocking minorities, though broader causal comparison is absent.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim is explicitly limited to enough actors on each side invoking exclusive divine title to prevent a divisible territorial settlement.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim requires only blocking minorities rather than universal belief, and the asserted mechanism closely matches the concrete reciprocal-entitlement example.

charityAssessment.alternative: Religious land claims may coexist with pragmatic compromise, and political, security, and national interests may independently obstruct settlement.
charityAssessment.decisiveQualification: The argument establishes a blocking mechanism among committed minorities, not that religion is the sole cause of the wider conflict.
charityAssessment.ratingRationale: By stressing that only enough actors are required, the move fairly avoids universal attribution, though it does not compare independent political causes.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Mutually exclusive absolute titles logically make division unacceptable, and committed minorities can plausibly block agreement; only the empirical power premise remains bounded.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The reciprocal Jewish and Muslim claims concretely illustrate the mechanism, but the political influence and settlement-blocking capacity of those minorities are not documented.

relevanceWithinTier.rationale: It directly supports the central religious-corruption bridge by showing how divine authorization can convert negotiable territory into absolute political entitlement.

pro-exclusive-divine-land-claims.evidenceBasis: The excerpt presents reciprocal Jewish and Muslim claims that God granted all the land exclusively to each side and says sufficient minorities can prevent a solution.
